subject: Nvidia's $1 Trillion U-Turn On Jensen Huang
body_text:

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Premarket trading: Anthropic ( ANT ) breaks below $83 IPO price .

 Self-driving race: Mercedes ( MBGAF ) wins edge over Tesla ( TSLA ).

 NATO intelligence: Russia plans to launch nuclear-armed satellite .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Complete turnaround 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 November 17: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted [Jensen Huang's] resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO after the disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms. While this was an unexpected transition, the board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company's employees, customers, partners and shareholders" - Harvey Jones, Nvidia Chairman of the Board 

 November 23: "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company" - Harvey Jones, Nvidia Chairman of the Board 

What's changed over the last week or two? A lot. The Nvidia ( NVDA ) board, led by Chairman Harvey Jones, has flip-flopped on its stance surrounding longtime leader Jensen Huang, issuing contradictory statements that baffled Wall Street. Both cited the best interests of stakeholders, but the board's lack of confidence over governance violations seemed to evaporate once an intervention was made on Jensen's behalf.

President Trump said he spoke "directly and indirectly" to Nvidia's board of directors to provide national security assurances and "convinced them." "You have to protect our geniuses, and we don't have enough of them," he told CNBC in an interview, adding that a thorough investigation was conducted. "This [case] is different because of the vast amount of knowledge in his brain. He's a national treasure." Silicon Valley cheers Jensen Huang's return 

 The aftermath: Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares soared 31% on the news on Monday, with the AI chip giant adding more than $1T in market cap to set a new market record. U.S. stocks also saw their best day since April 2025 , with the Nasdaq ( COMP:IND ) ending up a whopping 6.5%. Huang is still due to testify in front of Congressional committees next month, while an outside counsel will keep investigating foreign intelligence and export control allegations. In premarket trading this morning, Nvidia has pared some of the big gains, falling 5.5% to $156. ( 28 comments )
